name: PluginEvalSpec
description:
PluginEvalSpec says which plugin version is evaluated, on which models,
 how many times, and within what spend.

fields.name: PluginId
fields.description: ID of the plugin whose evals run.

fields.name: PluginDigest
fields.description:
The plugin version (archive digest) to evaluate. Empty evaluates the
 current version.

fields.name: Targets
fields.description:
The engines and models each case runs on, at most six. Empty runs
 each case on the model it names, or on the platform's default model.

fields.name: Runs
fields.description:
Tries per case, arm and target, from 1 to 50. Zero uses each case's
 own runs value, or 3.

fields.name: Ablation
fields.description: Whether each case also runs without the plugin, for comparison.

fields.name: Threshold
fields.description:
The score a case needs to pass, from 0 to 1, or 1 when unset: every
 scored check passes on every try.

fields.name: CaseGlob
fields.description:
Runs only the cases whose directory name matches this glob, as in
 "review-*". Empty runs every case.

fields.name: CaseTags
fields.description:
Runs only the cases carrying at least one of these tags. Empty runs
 every case.

fields.name: JudgeModel
fields.description:
The model AI-graded checks use. Empty uses the platform's default
 judge model.

fields.name: MaxCostUsd
fields.description:
The most this eval may spend, in estimated US dollars of model cost.

 Checked before each try starts, counting what tries already spent and
 the cap each running try still holds: tries already running and their
 AI-graded checks finish, so the spend can pass the limit by those.

fields.name: Concurrency
fields.description: Tries running at once, from 1 to 8. Zero means 1.

fields.name: AllowTools
fields.description:
Tools every try may use beyond each case's own list, in Claude Code's
 names, as Claude Code's --allow-tools.

 A specifier in parentheses, as in Bash(npm test *), is accepted and
 grants the whole tool: every Stigmer tool list reads a specifier that
 way. Each try runs in a fresh workspace of its own. A plugin's MCP tools
 are named either way: Claude Code's mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>
 or Stigmer's mcp__<server>__<tool>.

fields.name: RealMcpServers
fields.description:
Runs the plugin's MCP servers for real, with the organization's
 connections. Off by default: a try cannot call the plugin's MCP tools,
 as in Claude Code's evals without mocks.

fields.name: Vaults
fields.description:
Vaults whose logins and secrets the tries use, in order: the first
 vault holding a match wins. At most 20.

 A try has no person, so these vaults are all its hooks and servers
 use. Each is a shared vault: a My vault, the creator's included, is
 refused, because every viewer of the plugin may read a try, and a
 hook's or server's output can show what a key unlocked.
